transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining this medication safety huddle. As you know, the new intravenous anticoagulant protocol went live on Monday, and before I sign off on the afternoon decision for its use on the night shift, I need to hear from each of you. Pharmacy, laboratory medicine, nursing education, and clinical IT — please report any operational findings or concerns you've identified with the protocol, the automated dispensing cabinet stocking, or the electronic medication record ordering process. I'll review everything before making my final decision on any required safeguards.

transcript.text: I need to report a significant safety concern from pharmacy. Since Monday, I've verified three selection errors involving the 1 mg/mL and 2 mg/mL anticoagulant concentrations. To mitigate this risk, pharmacy can remove the bedside stock from the automated dispensing cabinets and instead supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes during a temporary hold. This would eliminate the concentration selection errors we're seeing at the point of use.

transcript.text: I need to report a laboratory medicine concern. Our anti-Xa analyzer is unavailable for calibration until Friday at 17:00. During that period, the laboratory's approved replacement for monitoring patients on this protocol is an aPTT test every six hours. This means we cannot provide anti-Xa level monitoring for patients receiving this anticoagulant until Friday evening, and any dosing adjustments will rely on aPTT results instead.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to report a nursing education concern. My competency roster shows that 18 nurses scheduled for tonight's shift have not completed the new anticoagulant administration module. Each of these nurses must receive charge-nurse sign-off before they are permitted to administer this medication. This is a significant staffing and competency gap that needs to be addressed before the protocol is used on the night shift.

transcript.text: From clinical IT, I can report that I've confirmed a high-priority electronic medication-record alert is ready to be deployed at 16:00 today. This alert will warn prescribers about concentration selection and require acknowledgment before the order can be released. Given the selection errors pharmacy has already identified, this electronic safeguard can serve as an additional layer of protection at the ordering stage.

decisions.safety_protocol: Temporary hold on the new intravenous anticoagulant protocol for the night shift, pending resolution of identified safety concerns.
decisions.dispensing_concentration: Remove bedside stock of both concentrations from automated dispensing cabinets; supply only pharmacy-prepared 1 mg/mL syringes to eliminate concentration selection errors at the point of use.
decisions.laboratory_monitoring: Anti-Xa monitoring unavailable until Friday 17:00; aPTT every 6 hours is the approved replacement, but this is a significant limitation for safe dosing adjustments and contributes to the decision to hold the protocol tonight.
decisions.nurse_authorization: 18 nurses on tonight's shift have not completed the required competency module; charge-nurse sign-off is required for each before administering the medication. This staffing and competency gap must be resolved before protocol use resumes.
decisions.electronic_alert: Deploy the high-priority electronic medication-record alert at 16:00 today as an additional safeguard at the ordering stage, requiring prescriber acknowledgment of concentration selection before order release.

commitments.detail: Remove both anticoagulant concentrations from automated dispensing cabinets and prepare only 1 mg/mL syringes from pharmacy during the temporary hold.
Notify clinical teams that anti-Xa monitoring is unavailable until Friday 17:00 and that aPTT every 6 hours is the interim monitoring method. Confirm when anti-Xa calibration is complete.
Ensure all 18 non-competent nurses complete the anticoagulant administration module and receive charge-nurse sign-off before being permitted to administer this medication.
Deploy the electronic medication-record concentration-selection alert at 16:00 today and confirm it is active before the protocol is reinstated.

Reconvene a medication safety review once anti-Xa monitoring is available, the electronic alert is live, nursing competency is resolved, and pharmacy-prepared syringes are in place before lifting the temporary hold.
